techniques: Hand Piecing, Hand Quilting, English Paper Piecing
project_story: I started this the winter after we lost the garden to the frost — I wanted something that felt like it was still blooming. Every hexagon is a fabric I'd been saving for a decade, some of it from your grandmother's scrap bin. It took the better part of a year, mostly stitched in the evenings while the news was on. I still find pins in the couch cushions.

techniques: Machine Piecing, Machine Quilting, Foundation Piecing
project_story: Made entirely from your father's old work shirts after he cleared out his closet. I couldn't bear to give them to the donation bin, so I cut them into strips instead. This one lives on the porch swing from May through October.
Made for the harvest table the year the co-op finally had a good crop. I designed the star layout myself on graph paper — first time I didn't work from someone else's pattern.
Every block uses fabric I dyed myself in the backyard vats last summer — thirty-one shades of blue, one for every day. Still on the design wall, still deciding on the border.

techniques: Hand Piecing, Hand Quilting, English Paper Piecing
project_story: Made for my sister's fortieth anniversary, using the actual template pieces our mother cut in 1968. The curves nearly broke me — I unpicked the whole top row twice before it lay flat. Margaret cried when she unwrapped it, and so did I.

Started the week your grandfather passed. I needed something with a lot of small, exacting steps to keep my hands busy. The geese all point north because that's the direction he always said the good weather came from.
A quick one, made in a weekend for the kitchen table. Sometimes you need a project that finishes before you lose interest.
Made for the first great-grandbaby. I wanted colors that would still look good in every photograph for the next eighty years, so I kept it simple — just red, yellow, and blue turning in circles.
The diamonds never wanted to match up and I put it in the closet in a fit of frustration. Ten years later it's still there. Maybe this is the year.
lessons_learned: Should have starched the bias edges before piecing. Every diamond point taught me a new way to swear quietly.

project_story: My very first quilt, made the year you were born, mostly at 2am while you slept. Every stitch is a little wobbly and I wouldn't change a thing about it.
lessons_learned: Learned to piece by candlelight during a very long winter and a lot of very short naps.

project_story: Made in the six weeks after retiring, when the house was finally quiet enough to hear the sewing machine think.
A housewarming gift I made for myself when I moved. Every new house deserves a star over the door, even if it just hangs in the hallway.
